POLICY & PROCEDURE FOR DISCHARGE:

1. POLICY:

  • A complete discharge summary is given to all the patients who are discharged from the hospital including MLC and DAMA, LAMA cases.
  • In case of DAMA, LAMA, consent is taken from the patient/ next of kin mentioning the reason for DAMA, LAMA.

2. PURPOSE:

To guide discharge process effectively.

3. SCOPE:

Hospital wide.

4. RESPONSIBILITY:

Nurses, primary consultant/RMO, Emergency medical officer.

5. DISTRIBUTION:

Front office, Nursing Administration, Medical administration, Emergency.

6. PROCEDURE:

6.1 Discharge of patient from the hospital can be classified as follows:

6.1.1 Normal discharge (Cash Discharge/ Insurance Discharge / Corporate Discharge)

6.1.2 Transfer

6.1.3 LAMA / DAMA (Leave / Discharge against Medical Advice)

6.1.4 Death

6.1.5 Discharge In case of Medico Legal Case

6.2.1 Normal Discharge Procedure:

  • Discharge Decision:

Decision regarding discharging the patients rest with the primary treating consultant of the patient who make such decision during his evening rounds on the previous day prior to the discharge of patient and the same is communicated to the patient, relatives ,the concerned ward nursing staff / on duty Medical Officer. However the final decision regarding discharge is made on the basis of the condition of the patient during the morning round of the primary consultant on the scheduled day of discharge.

On the scheduled day of discharge the primary treating consultant during his morning rounds examines the condition of the patient to ascertain whether the patient can be discharged. After conforming the patients fit to be discharged on that day the same is communicated to ward nurse and the medical officer on duty.

  • Preparation of Discharge Summary

After final decision to discharge the patient is taken, the treating consultant prepares the discharge summary of the patient which contains the following information:

    • Reasons for Admission
    • Investigations performed and summarized information about the results of the investigations
    • Diagnosis made
    • Record of any procedures (operation, etc) performed
    • Condition of the patient at the time of discharge
    • Medication instructions
    • Follow up Advice
    • Emergency contact number of the hospital

One copy of the Discharge Summary is handed over to the patient/relatives and the other copy is attached to the patient’s case file.

As per the instructions of the treating consultant in the Discharge Summary, patient relatives are advised by the Ward nurse to collect the medicine from the pharmacy as per the discharge medicines indicated by the treating consultant of the doctor.

    • Whenever discharges of patient is decided by a consultant, a complete Discharge summary with medications and follow up advice is written by Duty RMO.
    • Family members are informed accordingly by concern nurse and Doctor /RMO.
    • The whole billing card is rechecked by the RMO.
    • Bed charges & doctor consultation charges are made entry in the bill Card.
    • The investigation reports are rechecked.
    • Due report slip (if any) is prepared by RMO and the patient/patient’s NOK made signed on the same. One copy of Due slip is given to the patient and another copy is kept in the patient medical records. In case of TPA/Corporate patient the patient’s copy is sent to the billing counter.
    • Print out of medicine details are to be attached with the billing card for verifications of medicines indented & credited by sister.
    • Other details such as consumables used are checked whether made entries in the bill card.
    • OT entries are to be rechecked (if any).
    • Bed side procedure or any departmental procedures to be entered in the system.
    • Staff nurse send the unused medicine to the pharmacy using Medicine return slip along with the Bill card.
    • Then the pharmacy made the clearance in the Bill card and returns the same to the respective ward.
    • Sending the billing card with signature to the billing dept and intimating the patients’ relative.
    • In case of corporate and TPA patient, the original reports are to be send to IPD in-charge for submission to commercial department.
    • Indoor billing department provides final bill to the patient relative which contains detail breakup of all medical expenses.
    • In case of cash patient, after receiving full payment from the patient’s NOK, clearance for discharge is given from billing counter and same is handover to staff nurse by patient’s NOK.
    • In case of Insurance/Corporate cases, bills are settled accordingly after receiving of pre-authorization/ credit letters and the clearance for discharge is given to patient’s NOK.
    • All the documents e.g. discharge summery, investigation report are handed over to the patient by the staff nurses and after receiving the accounts clearance slip from the patient’s NOK.
    • Discharge summary is explained by Sister in charge/ staff nurse.
    • Feedback form is given to the patient at the day of discharge and collected from the patient after completing the whole discharge process by the RMO / Nurse.
      • The different types of Normal discharge are:
  • Cash Discharge: When the patient is paying by cash during discharge it is called cash discharge. Patient’s NOK are given final discharge bill. The balance amount is paid and the due is cleared. The patient’s NOK are handed over the Discharge bill for discharge with hospital stamp after clearance of all due amount, by which all the rest of the documents is handed over from the respective ward.
  • Credit Discharge :
  • Insurance Discharge: During cashless insurance discharge a valid authorization is mandatory. The authorization has to have the clause mentioned in the approval. If the full amount is granted by the insurance agency even then the standard non-reimbursable amounts to be paid by the patient’s NOK at the time of discharge. As per the clause mentioned in the authorization if some amount has to be collected from the patient, that amount is calculated and conveyed to the patient’s NOK. The deposit amount is then taken in cash and Discharge slip is generated. The patient’s NOK are provided with the duplicate detailed bill with hospital stamp. Original discharge bill are signed by the patient relative & then it is sent to commercial department with the credit letter attached.
  • Corporate Discharge: For corporate credit discharge, a corporate letter stating all the details of the clauses with the hospital is mandatory. All instructions should be clearly mentioned in the credit letter. After showing the detailed bill to the patient’s NOK, and verifying all the details according to the credit letter, patient is discharged. Discharge bill are signed by the patient relative & then it is sent to commercial department with the credit letter attached.

6.2.3 Transfer:

  • Transfer of patients from HOSPITAL to any other hospital is done as per doctor’s advice or if the facility is not available in the hospital. In this case discharge summary is handed over to patients for further reference to other hospitals.
      • Left Against Medical Advice (LAMA) / Discharge Against Medical Advice (DAMA) :
  • The process of LAMA/DAMA is initiated by the patient / patient’s NOK through verbal communication to the Primary Consultant /Duty RMO.
  • LAMA/DAMA is mentioned in the treatment sheet by the Primary consultant/ Duty RMO.
  • LAMA/DAMA form duly filled up by the patient’s NOK and to be counter signed by Nursing staff, operation manager and Administrator respectively.
  • In the billing card also, LAMA/DAMA is mentioned by the RMO / Nurse.
  • For rest of the discharge process follow planned discharge portion.
      • Death:
  • The death intimation is given by the Primary Consultant/Duty RMO to the patient’s NOK.
  • Death summary is mentioned in the treatment sheet by Duty RMO.
  • Verification of the spelling of the patient name, age, sex and address to be done by the patient’s NOK for preparation of the death certificate in hospital prescribed format.
  • Death Certificate to be prepared by duty RMO mentioning cause of death and handed over to the patient’s NOK after receiving the Clearance slip from billing department.
  • For rest of the discharge process follow planned discharge portion (excluding discharge summary portion).
      • Discharge In case of Medico Legal Case:
  • Medico legal form is filled by Medical Officer and details of the MLC is documented.
  • Police intimation will be given immediately by Medical Officer.
  • All investigation reports and evidential materials shall be preserved by staff

nurse on duty, and handed over to MRD for safe custody.

  • MLC on admission / LAMA / death will be documented & intimated to police.
  • In case of death of MLC body is handed over to police for further legal process.

POLICY & PROCEDURES FOR ABSCONDED CASES:

  • POLICY:

Patients, who have left the ward without staff’s knowledge for more than 2 hours, are to be considered as absconded from HOSPITAL. Staff of HOSPITAL shall ensure the intimation of the same to Security, Local Police station as well as to the next of Kin to avoid violence.

  • PURPOSE:

To provide guidance on the measures and actions to be taken and by whom, in the event of a patient being identified as Missing/Absconded in HOSPITAL.

  • SCOPE:

This Policy and Procedure is applicable for Inpatient services in the hospital.

  • RESPONSIBILITY:

All staff involved in patient care shall be responsible for the implementation of this policy.

  • DISTRIBUTION:

Medical administration, nursing administration, Operation, Security.

  • PROCEDURE:

6.1 Procedure for assessment of risk of absconding patients-

  • Patients identified as missing/absconding shall be assessed for any harm or posing any threat either to themselves or others.
  • Patient who has been assessed is likely to attempt significant self-harm or suicide based on all relevant information indicating the individual’s state of mind and medical history.
    • Procedure for management of absconding patients-
  • Search immediate area/bed area to establish whether a patient has taken belongings with them.
  • Assess whether the absconded patient pose any harm or threat to him or other.
  • Inform the security to alert the main entrance and exit.
  • Inform the RMO on duty who will provide/confirm clinical opinion regarding risk assessment.
  • Call in the telephone numbers furnished by the patient / Next of Kin at the time of admission, or as entered in the system.
  • Lodge an FIR in Local Police station in writing in hospital Letter Head, receipt copy to be maintained in patient file.
  • Complete Incident Form and document in patients medical records.

6.3 Procedure when absconded patient is found-

  • Seek information about patient’s condition and whether they intend to return to hospital.
  • If patient returns to the hospital or agrees to return then Medical or nursing assessment (as appropriate) shall be done and treatment shall be provided as required.
  • Immediate contact shall be made with the patient’s NOK.
  • Assess whether there is further risk of patient absconding.
  • If patient refuse to return to hospital then this shall be discussed by the Administrator and respective departmental staff like Manager Operations, Nursing staff, Security in- charge with the medical team or concerned consultant.
  • Complete the incident report form and document in the medical records of the patient.
  • The analysis report shall be communicated to all concerned.
